target.title: improve(matrix): prove lifecycle parity across substrates
target.body:
Closes #101054

## What Problem This Solves

Matrix QA's homeserver control was Tuwunel-specific and exposed only a restart callback, so maintainers could not express or compare cold start, idempotent start, restart, stop, and resume behavior across the Docker reference server and the in-process Crabline substrate.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one substrate-neutral lifecycle controller, wraps the existing Tuwunel harness, and adds a Crabline adapter that preserves stable identity and port semantics with bounded readiness checks. Both implementations execute the same five differential scenarios through the existing Matrix QA probe path. The Crabline package is declared explicitly as a QA extension development dependency.

## User Impact

No end-user Matrix runtime behavior or configuration changes. Maintainers gain executable parity proof for lifecycle behavior across real Tuwunel and Crabline substrates.

## Evidence

- Exact pushed head: `aa675874d7d7592e9912af5e68b5b790a76790f7`.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kww5q0met59cek3efpas6278`: `OPENCLAW_QA_MATRIX_LIFECYCLE_E2E=1 pnpm test extensions/qa-matrix/src/substrate/lifecycle.test.ts extensions/qa-matrix/src/substrate/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts` passed 2 real-substrate tests plus 4 unit tests; Tuwunel and Crabline each passed all five lifecycle scenarios.
- The same exact-head Testbox run completed full `pnpm check:changed` with exit 0 across shrinkwrap validation, typechecking, lint, dependency pins, guards, and import-cycle checks.
- Fresh branch autoreview thread `019f3879-ef8b-7df0-b710-c1547d0e491e` completed with no accepted or actionable findings.
- Direct dependency proof: the exact published `@openclaw/crabline@0.1.9` tarball exports `startMatrixServer` from both its JavaScript and TypeScript declaration entry points; the real Crabline scenario also passed.

Developed with AI assistance. A sanitized agent transcript is available but is not included without explicit approval.


### Hosted CI recovery

- The first head exposed two task-local gate failures: deadcode ownership for the new runtime files and dependency guard on redundant manifest/lock churn.
- The recovery head removes the redundant declaration (current `main` already resolves `@openclaw/crabline@0.1.9`), promotes lifecycle controls through `extensions/qa-matrix/api.ts`, and keeps lightweight runner discovery unchanged.
- Blacksmith Testbox reran the runtime API contract, lifecycle unit tests, real five-scenario Tuwunel/Crabline proof, and deadcode successfully. Fresh autoreview thread `019f3886-8d0a-77c0-8799-829a05da2b9e` is clean.
